title: Finite-time blowup for Navier–Stokes: OpenAI's Lean proof, built and checked

contributors.name: Bhattacharjee, Deep
contributors.affiliation: Formerly, Electro-Gravitational Space Propulsion Laboratory (EGSPL), Bhubaneswar, Odisha 751030, India

description:
OpenAI's Lean 4 proof of finite-time blowup for the forced three-dimensional Navier–Stokes equations (openai/NavierStokesAndEuler, commit f9e8bc5, Apache-2.0), unchanged, with a record of an independent build. The mathematics, the papers and the Lean code are OpenAI's; this archive adds no new proof.

For every viscosity ν > 0 the library proves alternatives (C), breakdown on ℝ³, and (D), breakdown on ℝ³/ℤ³, of Fefferman's official description of the Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem, as formalized in Google DeepMind's Formal Conjectures. The build record (10 October 2026, Lean v4.34.0-rc2) shows that both theorems depend only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, that the 816 files contain no sorry, native_decide or new axiom, and that the 16 definitions and both statements are identical, declaration by declaration, to Formal Conjectures at commit 8bf45ed. The README summarizes the discussion in arXiv:2610.08144 of where the Lean proof departs from the written paper. Whether the Clay Mathematics Institute awards the prize is for the Institute to decide.
notes: The proof, the papers and the Lean code are by OpenAI (upstream commits by Boris Alexeev). The independent build and the checks in verification/ were recorded by Deep Bhattacharjee (d.bhattacharjee@erl-forschung.de; itsdeep@live.com).
